messages:
alex: CI on main is red for test_scheduler::test_ordering_random_seed — started failing intermittently after the timing refactor. Logs show a deadlock/timeout in 30% of runs. Anyone looked into this?
ci-bot: build #4921 — tests/runtime/test_scheduler.py::test_ordering_random_seed — FAILED (flaky) — rerun available: /ci/4921
jasmin: omg saw this locally earlier, pretty sure it only happens under heavy load (many threads). Think there's a race with the reorder queue.
kevin: can you paste the failure snippet?
alex: here —
```
E   AssertionError: expected [1, 2, 3] == [2, 1, 3]
E   assert 1 == 2
tests/runtime/test_scheduler.py:48: AssertionError
  (in test_scheduler: ordering mismatch after concurrent enqueues)
```
lee: looks like nondeterministic ordering, probably due to atomicity assumption being broken after <timing.py> change. That sleep tweak to 0.001s could be hiding the race.
jasmin: reproduction steps I used: `pytest tests/runtime/test_scheduler.py::test_ordering_random_seed -k ordering -vv --maxfail=1` then run it in a tight loop with `--count=200`. ~30% fail rate for me.
kevin: possible quick fixes: 1) make the test deterministic by setting a fixed seed and single-thread path 2) add retry in test harness 3) fix the underlying concurrency by using an atomic insert or a lock. Prefer (3) but we need a hotfix on main.
alex: can someone bisect to find when it regressed? It started ~two weeks ago in the timing refactor PR.
kevin: starting git bisect locally now across last 50 commits, will report commit hash if found.
jasmin: meanwhile I can add a temporary flake marker for CI to reduce noise: `@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=2)` — agree? cc @eng-runtime for visibility
lee: prefer not to mask unless we have a plan; put it in staging only if needed.
kevin: bisect progress: suspect commit `c3f1a9d` — introduced `timing.adjust_granularity` change. That matches the PR alex mentioned.
alex: thanks. can someone try reproducing against that commit with stress runner? I can carve out time in an hour.
jasmin: quick test suggestion: run with `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1` and `-k ordering` to see if any warnings pop. Also try enabling single core (CPU affinity) — sometimes scheduling differences hide the issue.
kevin: confirmed reproduces reliably on `c3f1a9d` with `--count=500` for me. I'll open a small PR to add a lock around enqueue and run full test matrix.
lee: if the lock changes perf-critical code, annotate with benchmark and look into a lower-level fix afterwards.
alex: sounds good. For the immediate CI noise, jasmin can toggle reruns=1 on main until the fix lands?
jasmin: will put a staging-only flaky marker and a note in the PR.
ci-bot: mention: @oncall-eng-runtime, issue #1723 created: "flaky test_scheduler ordering after timing granularity change" — https://tracker/1723 :eyes:
alex: thanks all. keep updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
